security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:1:# GitLab Password Standards
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:8:This document outlines information security password standards intended to protect GitLab information systems and other resources containing confidential (Red and Orange) GitLab data from unauthorized use, where technically feasible.
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:24:Constructing secure passwords and ensuring proper password management is essential. GitLab's password standards are based, in part, on the recommendations by [NIST 800-63B](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html). To learn what makes a password truly secure, read this [article](https://medium.com/peerio/how-to-build-a-billion-dollar-password-3d92568d9277) or watch this [conference presentation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vudZnjp5Uq0&t=19183) on password strength.
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:28:### Password Requirements
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:32:- Password Reuse = No
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:33:- Password expiration = No
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:36:To make a secure password you can remember, consider using a [combination of 5 or more random words](https://medium.com/peerio/how-to-build-a-billion-dollar-password-3d92568d9277#67c2) or [generate in 1Password](/handbook/security/corporate/systems/1password/) and store. This helps ensure the password isn't easily guessable and will be unique across sites.
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:38:### Password Management
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:40:- Passwords are to be kept private and secured.
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:41:- Individual account passwords are not to be shared.
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:42:- Passwords are not to be stored in clear text or be written down.
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:43:- Password "hints" are not to be used. If a password is forgotten, a mechanism must be in place to replace a password/passphrase with sufficient controls to verify the identity of the requester of the password reset.
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:44:- Passwords must be stored in a way that is resistant to offline attacks and must be salted and hashed using a suitable one-way key derivation function.
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:45:- If a password is required to be stored, it must be stored within an approved password or secrets manager.
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:46:- If an account or password is suspected to have been compromised, immediately report the incident to Security and promptly follow instructions.
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:48:### System Password Configuration Requirements
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:50:- For systems where a password can be configured the minimum password length needs to be set to 12 characters.
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:52:- If a particular system requires a password history, configuration should be set for 25 remembered passwords.
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:53:- Passwords are not acceptable if they match the subsequent patterns, and must be checked against commonly used or expected patterns, including: known breached password lists, dictionary words, repetitive or sequential characters, or context specific words such as the name of the service, username, or derivatives thereof.
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:54:- System administrators of applications and/or devices must change default passwords.
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:55:- System administrators need to enable password strength on third party applications and/or tools, where applicable.
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:56:- For applications where a password is the only source of authentication, a password must be expired within a maximum of 90 calendar days.
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:67:Not all MFA methods offer equivalent protection. The key security distinction is **phishing resistance**: whether authentication is cryptographically bound to the relying party origin, making credentials impossible to replay against a spoofed site. 
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:76:| **High** | Synced Passkey | 1Password, iCloud Keychain, Chrome/Google Password Manager | Have + Are or Know ² | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | Sync account or vault compromise |
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:79:| **Low** | TOTP / Soft Token | Okta Verify OTP, Google Authenticator, 1Password TOTP | Have | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | AiTM real-time phishing, seed theft |
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:81:| **Not Permitted** | Security Question | Secret questions, account recovery prompts | Know | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | Guessing, social engineering, data breach exposure |
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:82:| **Not Permitted** | Password Hint | — | Know | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | Guessing, social engineering; by design reduces password entropy |
security__policies_and_standards__password-standard.md:90:For a better understanding of how MFA fits into GitLab, refer to the [Accounts and Passwords](/handbook/security/password-guidelines/) section, which includes pointers for setting up passwords, acquiring FIDO2 tokens, and links to further resources. Refer to the Tools and Tips page for more detailed information regarding [FIDO2/WebAuthn](/handbook/tools-and-tips/#fido2--webauthn) and [other 2FA methods](/handbook/tools-and-tips/#other-2fa-methods).

content.text: Treat a login password as highly sensitive. It should be kept private and never shared, written down, or stored in clear text. If it must be stored, use an approved password or secrets manager. Its classification is the same as the highest classification of the data it protects (data-classification-standard; password-standard).
